# Proposal output

When a runner returns proposals, the gate reports them three ways on the PR: the `pollux-agent` check run (`action_required`, listing doc paths and reasons), one review comment per proposal on the head commit, and one summary comment on the PR. A "no impact" result sets the check to `success` with the reason and posts no comments. Proposals are acted on from those comments (see [Apply and Skip](#apply-and-skip)).

## Failures and Re-run

Every analysis first creates an in-progress check and saves an armed run (nonce, 10-minute deadline), so a check is never missing or left pending: the deadline sweep closes any armed run neutral (see [Job queue](job-queue.md)). Any failure ends the check neutral, titled "Analysis failed" (or "PR too large to analyze"), with a one-line fixed cause that never quotes model output, provider responses, or artifact text; the detail stays in the server log. A superseded or interrupted analysis is not a failure: the next analysis closes its check as superseded.

A successful summary opens with "**pollux-agent** proposes N doc update(s)." (open proposals only) and has no Re-run box. After a failure the summary instead opens with the cause and ends with an unticked "- [ ] Re-run analysis". Proposals from an earlier successful run stay listed and are not marked outdated, because a failure says nothing about them. Ticking the box (an edited `issue_comment` on the bot's own summary, identified by the comment's App ID and its saved comment ID; a tick elsewhere, a comment from another App, or any other edit does nothing) or clicking GitHub's Re-run on the check (`check_run` `rerequested`) enqueues a `pull_request`-kind job. It fetches the PR's current head and starts a fresh analysis with a new check run, and the box is unticked when that analysis next writes the summary (on its result or its failure; an Actions re-run leaves it ticked until the workflow finishes). A re-run needs no permission check of its own: GitHub only lets people with write access tick another user's task box or re-run a check. A re-run of a closed PR, or a second one while an analysis of the same head is still running, does nothing, so repeated ticks cannot stack model runs.

A re-run waits for an analysis already running on the PR instead of cancelling it, and a push supersedes a re-run like any analysis, so only the newest head produces the final check; a same-head check it replaces reads "Superseded by a re-run". For forks, `check_run` may carry no pull request; the handler then finds the PR by the check's head SHA in stored state. Posting comments after a result is retried a few times with backoff, and a retry adopts comments already created by their markers, so nothing is duplicated.

## Apply and Skip

Anyone with write access can act on proposals; the sender's permission is checked through the GitHub API before anything else, and a sender without it gets a reply and a `confused` reaction. A comment that asks for nothing costs no GitHub call. The bot reacts `eyes` when it picks an action up and swaps that for `rocket` when done or `confused` when it refused with a reply saying why. A refused tick is unticked so it can be ticked again.

Each action has a checkbox and a command. Checkboxes are edits of the bot's own comments: "Apply this change" on a proposal's review comment, and "Apply all", "Skip this commit", "Skip this PR" on the summary. Commands are new issue comments (not review comments) whose first line starts with `/pollux-agent`: `apply` (all open proposals), `skip <reason>`, and `skip-pr <reason>`.

- **Apply.** Commits the open proposals it targets as one commit on the PR branch, without forcing: whole-section splices into each doc at the head, and for a new doc the file plus its entry in `docs/README.md`'s `## Index`. The commit message is `docs: apply pollux-agent proposal for <doc> § <section>`, or `docs: apply N pollux-agent proposals`. It is refused, with nothing committed, on a fork, on a closed PR, when the proposals were not made for the live head (a newer push is being re-analyzed, the last analysis failed, or the PR is skipped), when a section's original text no longer occurs exactly once in the doc, when the branch moved meanwhile, or when GitHub rejects the commit (a protected branch, a symlink or submodule at a doc path). On success each applied proposal becomes `applied` with the commit SHA, its box is ticked (for Apply all), its summary row shows the SHA, and an "Applied in <sha>" reply is posted under its comment; the summary reads "All proposals applied." when none are open. The pushed commit triggers a normal analysis, which keeps an applied proposal applied while the verdict repeats the same content; if everything is applied the check is `success` titled "Docs up to date".
- **Skip.** Passes the check as `success` titled "Skipped by @user" with the reason. "Skip this commit" covers only the head it was made at; "Skip this PR" covers every later push too, which concludes each new head as skipped without starting an analysis (so proposals are not refreshed). A skip command with no reason, or a skip tick, makes the bot ask for one; the asker's next comment on the PR becomes the reason, and a push before then cancels the ask with a note. Reasons are collapsed to one line, capped at 500 characters, and have `@` mentions and checkbox markup broken so they notify nobody and cannot pass for a box.

Apply is crash-safe. Before committing, the gate saves a pending apply (proposal IDs, message, parent SHA). If the commit landed but the state was not saved, the retry or the push of that commit (or a push on top of it) recognizes the bot's own commit by message and parent and adopts it; any other push drops the pending apply. A redelivered Apply only posts the ticks, summary and replies still missing, marked by `<!-- pollux-agent:applied:ID:SHA -->`.

## Where the section text comes from

Each proposal carries the current text of the section it replaces and that text's head-side line range in the doc. The server runner fills both from its own checkout of the head commit (see [Server runner](server-runner.md)); the Actions runner fills them from the doc fetched at the head SHA through the contents API (see [Actions runner](actions-runner.md)); they are never model output and are kept out of the generated JSON schema. Both are empty for a new doc. The range runs from the heading through the section's last line, including trailing blank lines. The gate may import only `internal/review`, so it cannot parse docs itself; it trusts these fields. A proposal whose doc or section is missing at the head, or whose heading matches more than one section, leaves them empty, and its comment degrades to the checkbox variant; guessing the section would let a suggestion overwrite the wrong one.

A proposal's content replaces the whole section, heading line included, because a suggestion replaces the heading line too. Both runner prompts and the generated schema say so. If the content still starts without a heading of the section's level, the gate puts back the original heading and the blank lines after it before rendering; otherwise applying the edit would delete the heading from the doc. A proposal's `doc_path` must end in `.md` or `.mdx`.

## Two comment variants

- **Suggestion.** Used only when the whole section, trailing blank lines included, lies inside one head-side hunk of that doc in the PR diff. GitHub only accepts review comments on diff lines, so this is the one case where the comment can sit on the doc's own lines. It is a GitHub `suggestion` block replacing exactly those lines, with the reason and no checkbox. The suggestion restates the section's trailing blank lines, otherwise applying it would eat the gap before the next heading. The code fence is made longer than any backtick run in the content so proposed code fences cannot close it early.
- **Checkbox.** Used for everything else: the doc is not in the diff, the section only partly overlaps a hunk or spans two, or the doc is new. The comment sits on the proposal's anchor line (a changed code line) and holds the reason, the doc path and section, the edit as a `diff` block (old section lines `-`, new lines `+`; a new doc shows only added lines plus its index entry), and an unticked "Apply this change" task-list item.

## Identity and re-runs

A proposal's identity is its doc path plus its normalized section heading (leading `#` and whitespace stripped; path alone for a new doc), hashed to a short ID. The gate remembers each proposal's ID, comment ID and URL, and state (`open`, `outdated`, or `applied`), plus the summary comment ID, per PR.

On each run, after the check run is created, the gate reconciles the new proposals against what it remembers:

- **Same proposal again:** its comment is edited in place. The PR's comment count does not change across pushes.
- **New proposal:** a new review comment.
- **Proposal gone:** its comment and summary row are marked `outdated`; the old body stays readable under an "Outdated" notice. The gate never deletes a comment: that would erase the thread's replies and history, and a proposal that returns would have to start over. A proposal that returns after being outdated reopens its old comment. An applied proposal stays applied.
- **No impact:** every earlier open proposal is marked outdated and the check is `success`.
- **Summary:** one issue comment listing every proposal with doc path, section, a link to its comment, and state, plus the Skip boxes. It is edited in place, and only created when there is something to list or one already exists.

A comment keeps its location and variant across edits. GitHub cannot move a review comment, and replacing it would churn the thread. A suggestion block on the wrong lines would overwrite them when applied, so on edit the suggestion body is used only if the existing comment already sits on that doc at the same lines; otherwise the body is the checkbox variant. If a user deletes a proposal's comment, an open proposal gets a fresh comment, and an outdated one is skipped rather than resurrected.

## Markers and crash recovery

Every proposal comment starts with a hidden `<!-- pollux-agent:proposal:ID -->` and the summary with `<!-- pollux-agent:summary -->`. The gate lists the PR's comments before writing and, when its stored state lacks a comment ID, adopts the comment carrying the marker. It adopts or edits only comments written by the App's own bot user, with the marker as the body's first line: anyone can paste a marker into a comment (proposal IDs are hashes of public data), and adopting theirs would make every later edit fail with 403. So if a run stops after GitHub accepted a comment but before the gate saved its ID, the next run reuses that comment instead of posting a second. Before its first create, a run saves the proposals it is about to post, so even a run that crashed on its very first post leaves state behind; the next run then lists comments and adopts or outdates them, including when it finds no impact. State is saved again after all writes succeed. The concluded state (check done, run cleared) is saved before comments are posted, so a comment failure cannot leave an armed run for the deadline sweep to overwrite a success with neutral. Any other failed run is redone by the next push or re-run (see [Job queue](job-queue.md)).

## Known limits

- If a later push deletes the anchor line, GitHub shows its own "Outdated" badge on a still-open proposal; the gate's state is unaffected.
- The two GitHub comment APIs (review and issue) have separate ID spaces and edit endpoints, so the gate tracks which kind each comment is.
- Apply is unavailable on a fork the bot cannot push to; the comments say so instead of offering the box.

proposals.content:
## Guarantees

- **Deduplicated by delivery.** A repeated `X-GitHub-Delivery` ID is acknowledged and changes nothing, including after a restart.
- **One job per PR at a time.** Jobs share a key (`owner/repo#number`); jobs with the same key run in order, one at a time, and different PRs run in parallel up to a fixed cap.
- **Newer push wins.** A `pull_request` job supersedes older jobs with the same key and kind: pending ones are skipped, a running one has its context cancelled. Jobs of other kinds are not affected. A re-run (see [Proposal output](proposal-output.md)) is a `pull_request`-kind job too but does not supersede: it queues behind a running analysis on the same key, so it never cancels one and then skips. A later push still supersedes a queued or running re-run, so only the newest head produces the final check.
- **Job kinds.** `pull_request` (supersedes), `comment` (an Apply, Apply all, or Skip action, or a skip reason, from a comment; it never supersedes, so it queues behind a running analysis on the same key and an Apply sees settled state), `workflow_run` (an Actions analysis run finished), and `run_deadline` (an awaited run passed its deadline). A sweep every 30 seconds enqueues one `run_deadline` job per overdue awaited run; its delivery ID is `deadline:<nonce>` plus the current minute, so sweeps within a minute dedupe and a deadline job whose GitHub write was rejected is retried the next minute until the check is closed. A deadline job for a run that has since completed or been replaced by a new push does nothing.
- **At least once.** A job running at shutdown or crash stays `running` and is requeued on the next start, so it can run twice. Every handler must be safe to repeat for the same payload; Apply keeps a pending-apply record so a repeated or crashed one adopts its own commit instead of committing twice.
- **No job-level retry.** A failed job is recorded with its error and not retried; the next push or re-run for the PR replaces it. The only retry is the deadline job, which backstops a check left in progress: it is re-enqueued with exponential backoff (about 0, 1, 2, 4, 8 … 1024 minutes past the deadline, then every 4 hours) and given up, with a warning in the log, once the run is a day overdue.

## Events

Subscribe to: Pull request, Pull request review comment (a ticked "Apply this change" box on a proposal's comment), Issue comment (new comments carrying `/pollux-agent apply`, `skip <reason>` or `skip-pr <reason>` commands or a skip reason; edits that tick "Re-run analysis", "Apply all", "Skip this commit", or "Skip this PR" on the summary comment), Check run (GitHub's Re-run on the `pollux-agent` check), Workflow run (tells the backend a dispatched analysis run finished). proposals.content:
---
title: Deploying pollux
summary: Run pollux on one host with Docker Compose and let a systemd timer deploy new commits of main.
covers:
  - Dockerfile
  - compose.yaml
  - .dockerignore
  - deploy/**
---

# Deploying pollux

The production deploy is one host running the backend under Docker Compose. A systemd user timer redeploys whenever `origin/main` moves. For configuration values see [Registering the GitHub App](github-app.md) and [Setup](setup.md); for how the parts fit see [Architecture](../architecture.md).

## Image

The `Dockerfile` builds `cmd/server` and `cmd/healthcheck` as static binaries and copies them into a distroless `nonroot` image. The image has no shell or curl, which is why the health probe is its own binary: it does a GET and passes only on status 200. `.dockerignore` excludes everything but `backend/`, and keeps databases, `.env` files and `.pem` keys out of the build context.

## Compose service

- Configuration comes from `.env` in the repo root. `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE` in `.env` must be set to the host path of the App's private key; compose refuses to start without it and bind-mounts it read-only into the container, where the server reads it from `/run/secrets/github-app.pem`.
- The SQLite database lives on the `pollux-data` volume at `/data/pollux.db`. It holds the job queue, so keep the volume across deploys.
- The container is hardened: read-only root file system with a `tmpfs` at `/tmp`, all capabilities dropped, `no-new-privileges`.
- Port 8080 is published on `127.0.0.1` only. Put a reverse proxy or tunnel in front of it to receive GitHub webhooks.
- The health check calls `/healthz` every 30s, and every 2s during a 10s start period, so `docker compose up --wait` returns as soon as the server is healthy.
- `stop_grace_period` is 20s so in-flight work can finish; unfinished jobs resume after a restart (see [Job queue](../features/job-queue.md)).

## Auto-update

`deploy/pollux-update.timer` starts `deploy/pollux-update.service` one minute after boot and every 2 minutes after that. The service runs `deploy/pollux-update.sh` from the checkout at `~/pollux-agent`, so clone the repo there.

The script:

1. Takes a lock so overlapping runs exit quietly.
2. Fetches `origin/main`. It does nothing when that commit is already deployed, or is the commit that last failed.
3. Switches the checkout to the commit and runs `docker compose up -d --build --wait`.
4. On success, records the commit as deployed.
5. On failure, records the commit as failed, so the timer does not retry a commit that builds but never turns healthy, and rolls back to the previously deployed commit if there is one. The next merge to `main` clears the failed marker by moving the target.

title: Deploying
summary: Run pollux on one host with Docker Compose and how the auto-update timer deploys and rolls back.
covers:

  - compose.yaml

# Deploying

pollux runs on a single host as one container built from this repo. A systemd timer on that host deploys `origin/main` whenever it moves. For local development see [Setup](setup.md); for the App and its key see [Registering the GitHub App](github-app.md).

## Container

- The `Dockerfile` builds the server and a small `healthcheck` binary into a distroless image that runs as non-root. The image has no shell or curl, which is why the health probe is its own binary.
- `compose.yaml` runs it with a read-only root file system, a tmpfs `/tmp`, all capabilities dropped, and `no-new-privileges`.
- The port is published on `127.0.0.1:8080` only; put a reverse proxy in front for GitHub's webhooks.
- Configuration comes from a `.env` file next to `compose.yaml` (variables in [Setup](setup.md)). `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE` in `.env` must be the host path of the key; compose bind-mounts it read-only and points the container at the mounted copy. Compose refuses to start if it is unset. `DATABASE_PATH` and `ADDR` are fixed by compose.
- The SQLite database lives in the `pollux-data` volume at `/data`, so it survives rebuilds.
- The health check calls `GET /healthz` and passes only on 200. `docker compose up --wait` blocks until the container is healthy.

## Auto-update

`deploy/pollux-update.timer` starts `deploy/pollux-update.service` one minute after boot and then every 2 minutes. The service runs `deploy/pollux-update.sh` from the `pollux-agent` checkout in the user's home directory.

Each run:

1. Takes a lock, so overlapping runs do nothing.
2. Fetches `origin/main`. If it equals the last deployed commit or the last failed commit, it exits.
3. Checks out that commit detached and runs `docker compose up -d --build --wait`.
4. On success, records the commit as deployed.
5. On failure, records the commit as failed so the timer does not retry it, rebuilds the previously deployed commit if there is one, and exits non-zero. The next merge to `main` clears the failed state.

State lives in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/pollux` (default `~/.local/state/pollux`).

proposals.content:
## Skip

Skip has two scopes: this commit (the check passes for the current head; the next push is analyzed again) and this PR (the check passes for every later push and no analysis runs).

Ticking a Skip box does not skip yet. The bot asks that user for a reason, and their next comment on the PR becomes the reason; only then is the skip recorded. The command form with a reason takes effect at once, and without a reason gets the same ask. The check and the summary show who skipped, the scope, and the reason. A skip passes the check for the head it was made on; a commit skip is cleared by the next push. If a push to a new head arrives while either kind of skip is still waiting for its reason, the ask is cancelled and the bot says so in a comment, asking the user to tick again, so a skip never carries over to code the user has not seen. A redelivery of the same head keeps the ask, and the note is posted once the new head is saved, even if that push's analysis fails. A Re-run on a new head does the same.

The reason is for people: it is stored collapsed to one line (control and bidi characters dropped) and capped at 500 characters. Every time it is shown in the summary or the check run it goes through the same inert-prose rendering as model-written reasons (see [Proposal output](proposal-output.md)), so it cannot ping anyone, link, embed, open HTML, link an issue, or pose as a checkbox. A redelivery of a skip stored by an older version, whose reason held zero-width spaces, still matches and does not redo the skip. The skip is saved before the summary is redrawn, so a failed redraw cannot leave the check green with no record; a redelivery redraws it. Skip needs the same write access as Apply and is allowed on forks. Nothing undoes a skip or an apply.

proposals.content:
## Inert model text

Everything the model writes that the gate echoes (reasons, doc paths, sections, index entries, the no-impact reason) is untrusted, so it is rendered so it cannot act as Markdown. A reason is collapsed to one line (control, bidi and zero-width-space characters dropped), capped at 1000 characters, and escaped: `@` mentions, `://` and `www.` autolinks, links and images, HTML and entities, issue references (`#N`, `GH-N`), unbalanced backticks, and a leading block marker (heading, quote, list, rule, fence, checkbox) are all broken, while balanced inline code spans are kept as written. Doc paths, sections and index entries are shown as a single code span whose delimiter is longer than any backtick inside; in the summary table's cells a `|` is also escaped so the row keeps its four cells. The check run summary uses the same rendering and lists paths as code spans; when the list would exceed the check run size limit it stops with "… and N more" instead of cutting through a code span.

## Two comment variants

- **Suggestion.** Used only when the whole section, trailing blank lines included, lies inside one head-side hunk of that doc in the PR diff. GitHub only accepts review comments on diff lines, so this is the one case where the comment can sit on the doc's own lines. It is a GitHub `suggestion` block replacing exactly those lines, with the reason and no checkbox. The suggestion restates the section's trailing blank lines, otherwise applying it would eat the gap before the next heading. The code fence is made longer than any backtick run in the content so proposed code fences cannot close it early.
- **Checkbox.** Used for everything else: the doc is not in the diff, the section only partly overlaps a hunk or spans two, or the doc is new. The comment sits on the proposal's anchor line (a changed code line) and holds the reason, the doc path and section (each as a code span), the edit as a `diff` block (old section lines `-`, new lines `+`; a new doc shows only added lines plus its index entry), and an unticked "Apply this change" task-list item.

proposals.content:
# Proposal output

When a runner returns proposals, the gate reports them three ways on the PR: the `pollux-agent` check run (`action_required`, listing doc paths and reasons), one review comment per proposal on the head commit, and one summary comment on the PR. A "no impact" result sets the check to `success` with the reason and posts no comments. The checkboxes act on the proposals; see [Apply and Skip](apply-skip.md). The summary also carries the PR-wide "Apply all", "Skip this commit", and "Skip this PR" checkboxes, drawn from stored state on every redraw (the bot never draws "Apply all" ticked: once a proposal is applied and none is open, the line becomes "✅ All proposals applied."), each proposal's applied state, and, on a fork PR, a notice that Apply is unavailable (proposal comments then have no Apply checkbox).

Model-written text is rendered inert everywhere it appears (review comments, summary, check run), so a hostile reason or doc path cannot ping anyone, link, embed an image, open HTML, decode an entity, link an issue or PR (`#N`, `GH-N`), or forge an Apply checkbox:

- **Reasons** (proposal and no-impact) are collapsed to one line, stripped of control, bidi and zero-width-space characters, capped at 1000 characters, and escaped: `@`, `://`, `www.`, `#N`, `GH-N`, `<`, `&`, brackets and backslashes are broken or escaped, and a leading block marker (heading, quote, list, rule, fence) is escaped. Balanced inline code spans in a reason stay as written; other backticks are escaped.
- **Identifiers** (doc path, section, index entry) are each shown as one inline code span, with a delimiter longer than any backtick run inside. In the summary table the pipes are escaped so the text stays in its cell.
- The check run's proposal list stops before the summary size limit with a "… and N more" line, so truncation never cuts through a code span.

proposals.content:
## Flow

1. A push to a PR reaches the gate. It dispatches the workflow on the **default branch**, passing the head SHA, PR number, and a fresh nonce. Dispatching the default branch's copy means a PR cannot change the workflow, its tools, or its secrets.
2. GitHub returns the run ID. The gate stores the run ID, nonce, head SHA, and a deadline on the PR's state and puts the check in progress.
3. The workflow checks out the head commit and runs Claude Code, then uploads a result artifact (always, even on failure).
4. A `workflow_run` completed event arrives. The run ID maps to its PR.
5. The runner downloads the artifact. The gate accepts it only if the run is the one dispatched for the PR's current head and the artifact's head SHA and nonce match.
6. Proposals outside `docs/` or not matching the schema are rejected, as is a result with no proposals and an empty or blank `no_impact_reason`. Otherwise the same transition as the server runner concludes the check: success ("No doc impact" with a reason) or action_required with the proposals.

proposals.reason: An existing branch with a pull request is no longer force-reset: a bot's PR is adopted and a human's PR fails the attempt.
proposals.content:
## Opening the PR

The branch `pollux-agent/docs-scaffold` is created off the default tip, with one commit and one PR into the default branch. If the branch already exists at another commit, pollux checks for a PR opened from it before touching it, because resetting the branch would close that PR. A PR opened by a bot (the App) is adopted. A PR opened by anyone else fails the attempt with an error naming it, and the branch is left alone. Only a branch with no PR is force-reset to the default tip before committing, so a PR is never opened from content pollux did not commit. When several PRs exist from the branch, an open one is preferred over closed ones. The validated files are stored as soon as they are written, so a failed commit or PR step retries without running the model again. A crash after the branch or PR exists is recovered by adopting them, not creating duplicates; a PR found after a failed create is adopted only if a bot opened it.

Any failure before the PR exists, including a workflow run that fails, is cancelled, or passes its deadline, leaves the repo's state retryable. Waiting checks then say an attempt failed, and the next PR event on a docs-less PR tries again. After 3 failed attempts the scaffold stops for good and the checks say it could not be written, so `docs/` has to be added by hand.
